text: Innisfree (Korean: 이니스프리) is a South Korean cosmetics brand owned and founded by Amore Pacific in 2000, marketed as the company's first eco-friendly brand. The brand name comes from W. B. Yeats' poem, 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'. Innisfree is known for its affordability and brand concept that emphasizes healthy, reasonably priced beauty products with ingredients responsibly sourced from Jeju Island, South Korea. It is South Korea's first all-natural brand and offers products ranging from makeup to skincare for women and men. The brand was launched by Amore Pacific, the largest skincare and cosmetics company in South Korea. Innisfree opened its first brand road-shop in 2005 and its 100th in 2007. The brand's first flagship store opened in Shanghai on April 25, 2012. In 2013, the company expanded to Hong Kong, Singapore, and India, opening its first Indian store in New Delhi on October 10, 2013, and its first Singaporean store on November 22, 2013. By 2014, Innisfree had over 80 stores in South Korea, Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and India. In the first half of 2014, Amore Pacific planned to boost sales in Taipei, opening a second store in Taiwan after launching there, aiming to make Innisfree the country's biggest South Korean skincare and cosmetics brand. On December 5, 2014, Innisfree opened its first store in Malaysia. In its fifteenth year, the brand launched in Thailand and opened its largest flagship store at Hongyi Square in Shanghai, China, with over 108 stores in the country by the end of the year. The first store in Vietnam opened in November 2016, and the first store in the Philippines opened two years later. On March 23, 2017, Innisfree opened its first store in Indonesia at Central Park Jakarta. The brand entered the halal market on November 25, 2024, after receiving certification from the Indonesian Halal Product Assurance Agency (BPJPH). In 2017, Innisfree expanded into North America, launching its first store in the United States on September 15, 2017, in Manhattan, followed by another location in Manhattan on October 5, 2018. However, in May 2021, Amore Pacific announced that all North American Innisfree stores would close due to the negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, though products remained available via Sephora. Innisfree entered the Australian market in 2018, opening its first retail outlet at Melbourne Central on June 6 and a second location in Sydney's Queen Victoria Building later that year, as part of a strategic effort to tap into Oceania's demand for skincare and cosmetics. The brand has also developed its own e-commerce website to enhance accessibility and consumer engagement in Australia. In 2011, Innisfree reported 140.5 billion won ($123.1 million) in sales from its 434 locations in South Korea. In 2019, sales revenue was 552 billion won (~$490.6 million), down from 600 billion (~$533.3 million) in 2018. In 2020, the brand reported its lowest net profit since 2013: approximately 10.22 billion won (~$9.06 million), down from about 48.87 billion won (~$43.3 million) in 2019. In 2023, Innisfree reported a net profit of approximately 10.3 billion won, a 68.2% decrease compared to the previous year, with India experiencing a 25% year-on-year growth, contributing to Amorepacific Group's overall 50% growth in the country. The brand uses the slogan "Clean Island, where clean nature and healthy beauty coexist happily" and emphasizes nature and eco-friendly practices. Since its launch in 2010, Innisfree has been endorsed by numerous celebrities, with its first model being Han Chae-young. Other endorsers include Kim Tae-hee, Nam Sang-mi, Song Hye-kyo, Moon Geun-young, Yoona, Lee Min-ho, Twice, Loona, Wanna One, Shin Ye-eun, and Ahn Hyo-seop. In 2021, singer-songwriter Stella Jang became an Innisfree model. In 2023, the brand unveiled Shin Ye-eun as its brand model through a promotional video for its annual "Inni-Super-Big-Sale" event. Ive (former Iz*One) member Jang Won-young is the brand's global ambassador. In February 2023, Mingyu of Seventeen was appointed as the next global model. In 2020, Innisfree released a repackaged version of the Green Tea Seed Serum labeled "HELLO, I'M PAPER BOTTLE". In April 2021, a customer accused the brand of "greenwashing" after posting photos and comments on Facebook revealing the product was in a plastic bottle, leading to a viral consumer backlash in local media. Innisfree issued a public apology, acknowledging the labeling may be misleading, and clarified that the packaging is recyclable, with the "paper bottle" referring to the paper label surrounding the bottle.
